newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung favourably reviews investment in Fokker.
newsitem.headline: Samsung favourably reviews investment in Fokker.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries said on Friday it was favourably reviewing a Dutch government proposal to take over bankrupt Dutch plane maker Fokker NV.
"The Dutch government is demanding a $500-600 million long-term investment in Fokker and we are favourably reviewing the proposal," a Samsung spokesman said.
"We are undertaking negotiations with the Dutch government in a very amicable, positive manner but no agreement has been reached yet," the spokesman said.
He denied a domestic newspaper report that Samsung had agreed in principle to take over Fokker for $150 million.
Samsung Aerospace, a unit of Samsung Group, wants to assemble aircraft developed by Fokker for sale in Asia, with the Dutch firm continuing to market for Europe, he added.
He said any agreement would be subject to approval by the Dutch parliament and the South Korean government.

The Dutch government on Friday said it had no comment on news from Samsung Aerospace that the government wanted an input of $500-600 million from the South Korean company to acquire plane maker Fokker.
"We are making no announcements on this," Luuc van Zijp, spokesman for Economics Ministry told Reuters.
He added that as far as he was aware, there were no press conferences planned for Friday on the Fokker takeover.
A spokesman for the Fokker receivers was not immediately available for comment.
